A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NIN/NeuroMFA research despite the changed title and organization. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v4 reports original analyses of Pythia checkpoints and diffusion-model networks, including multifractal spectra, emergence trajectories, sensitivity experiments, and empirical scaling fits.

after.justification: v5 retains original NeuroMFA analyses and adds toy-network experiments, ResNet analyses, Pythia data comparisons, and contaminated-training experiments with BERT.

M1.justification: v4 uses thresholded inverse weights and primarily next-layer neighborhood counts, with separate multilayer analyses. v5 Eqs. 1-2 introduce a path-length penalty, lambda times path length raised to gamma, and distance-threshold neighborhoods. This substantively changes the geometry entering NeuroMFA, although the partition-function, spectrum, and emergence-formula pipeline remains.

E1.justification: v5 Appendix C.3 adds BERT evaluation on SQuAD 1.1 reading comprehension and MultiNLI entailment under deliberately contaminated training using Wikipedia and random data. These introduce additional tasks and a degradation scenario beyond v4's training-progress evaluations. The existing Pythia benchmarks and diffusion analysis remain.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates a competing emergence-analysis method against NeuroMFA. Added BERT and ResNet models are subjects of structural analysis; the added task metrics validate correspondence with performance. Newly cited emergence methods are discussed without comparative experimental results.

E3.justification: v5 adds a BERT fine-tuning protocol with 20% Wikipedia data and 80% normally distributed random data, evaluated using SQuAD F1 and MultiNLI accuracy. It also introduces matched Pythia-standard/deduped comparisons and normalized cross-model comparisons at checkpoints 512 and 53,000. The explicit 64-node sampling statement clarifies an existing option rather than establishing a changed sampling budget.

E4.justification: v5 adds toy-network heterogeneity/regularity tests, CNN analyses, deduplication comparisons, and contaminated-training degradation tests in Appendices A.2.4 and C. Conversely, v4's alternative weight-transfer functions and one/two/three-layer sensitivity analyses disappear. The weighted-degree and log-log-fit analyses are retained and relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions average 10 sampled networks and report means and standard deviations for scaling fits. v5 identifies spectral shading explicitly as standard deviation and adds variance tables for alpha, f(alpha), alpha0, and spectrum width. This extends uncertainty documentation without establishing additional runs or a new seed design.

E6.justification: New findings include declining emergence and task scores during contaminated BERT training, differing standard/deduped Pythia trajectories, and ResNet spectral behavior. Tables 7-8 also report previously unshown WinoGrande scores. Transfer-function and layer-depth sensitivity results are removed. Many earlier plots remain, and v4 Table 2's scaling-fit values are unchanged in v5 Table 9; no same-setting performance improvement is established.

T1.justification: v5 revises formal distance and neighborhood definitions and adds an algorithmic-complexity derivation yielding O(LD^2), equivalently O(ND), under its stated simplifications in Appendix B.4. The scale-invariance lemmas, sampling argument, multifractal transformations, and Turing-pattern derivation remain. The explicit regression formula elaborates the previously specified estimator.

C1.justification: The central NIN, NeuroMFA, and emergence-metric contributions remain. v5 qualifies the metric as a structural proxy for emergent abilities and emphasizes structural emergence in large models. Its conclusion drops v4's speculation about identifying an AGI threshold.

C2.justification: v5 explicitly acknowledges that the emergence-performance relationship is correlational, without established causality, in its final limitations paragraph. It adds interpretations concerning architecture-dependent self-organization and effects of training-data quality, substantially expands the neuroscience analogy, and replaces v4's claim of lower CV-model intelligence with language about lower emergent abilities.

D1.justification: v5 clarifies that transformer analysis uses static WQ, WK, and WV matrices, specifies 64 sampled nodes per layer for the main experiments and lambda=1/gamma=5, and documents the BERT configuration and contamination mixture. The documented anonymous code repository identifier changes from Neuron_LLM-8738 to Neuron_LLM-4DC8. Existing Pythia configuration tables and core pseudocode remain.

R1.justification: v5 substantially expands positioning around network neuroscience, including Bullmore and Sporns and Bassett and Sporns. Related work adds Chen et al.'s entropy-based emergence analysis and Du et al.'s pretraining-loss perspective, while removing v4's discussion of essential sparsity, flipped in-context labels, and several domain-specific limitations studies.

P1.justification: v5 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, related work, and conclusion around structural analysis and neuroscience. It reorganizes methodological motivation and appendices, adds an appendix contents page, and moves the weighted-degree discussion and main-text algorithms into appendices. The title and author information also change.

P2.justification: v5 redesigns Figure 1, adds legends and revised axes styling to the main performance-comparison plots, and introduces radar charts, toy-network illustrations, additional experiment plots, and variance/performance tables. The earlier sensitivity figures disappear, while many retained plots move or shrink within the new single-column main-text layout.

improvement.justification: Compared with v4's predominantly training-progress evidence, v5's toy-network tests and BERT degradation experiment better examine what the metric tracks. More explicit uncertainty reporting, implementation information, and the causal limitation improve assessability. These gains are tempered by removing weight-transfer and layer-depth sensitivity evidence while revising the distance construction; the connection to emergent abilities remains correlational.
